name: HD 181327 debris ring
description: The debris ring around HD 181327 as JWST/NIRCam imaged it at 1.8 micrometres behind the MASK335R coronagraph on 11 October 2023 (programme 2780), in the colours and scale Gáspár et al. (2026) print it in. One unit is one astronomical unit; the ring's depth is the inclined ring that best projects to the image, not a measurement.

lenses.title: The debris ring around HD 181327 at 1.8 micrometres
lenses.summary: Starlight scattered by a ring of debris about 80 au from the star, in the paper's own colours and scale; its depth is the tilted ring that fits the image.
lenses.description: JWST/NIRCam imaged this star on 11 October 2023 with the F182M filter, 1.8 micrometres, behind the MASK335R coronagraph, which blocks the star so the faint ring of colliding debris around it shows. This is MAST's own coronagraphy product, which this project also re-ran from the archived exposures and compared. It is drawn in the colours and on the logarithmic scale Gáspár et al. (2026) print it in (their Figure 26), so seen from Earth it should look like their panel. The ring is starlight scattered by dust about 80 au out, tilted about 30° from face-on, with a fainter halo of small grains outside it. The image has no third axis, so its depth is inferred: a tilted ring of the geometry measured on it projects to the image better than a spherical shell or a constant depth, and each line of sight is placed on that ring. Which side is nearer to us, and how thick the ring is, are stated conventions. Nothing is drawn within 1 arcsecond of the star, where the starlight left after subtraction outweighs the dust; the star itself is the sphere at the centre.
lenses.innerMaskSource: Where this project's re-run of the pipeline and MAST's own product agree. Between 0.5 and 1 arcsec the two independent PSF subtractions of the same exposures correlate at only 0.46 to 0.86 across the six bands, so the light there is residual starlight that differs from band to band; from 1 to 2 arcsec they correlate at 0.89 to 0.99 (compare.mts receipts beside programs/hd-181327-2780.json). The MASK335R occulter itself reaches half transmission at 0.63 arcsec (CRDS jwst_nircam_psfmask_0211.fits).
